story.title: On the Piste in Dakar: Omani Fencer Jana Al Sharji Steps Onto the Youth Olympic Stage
story.seo_title: Omani Fencer Jana Al Sharji at Dakar Youth Olympics | OmanSpire
story.meta_description: Omani épée fencer Jana bint Mohammed Al Sharji makes her Youth Olympic Games debut at Dakar 2026 after winning two U-17 World Cup silver medals.

detail.extracted_title: On the Piste in Dakar: Omani Fencer Jana Al Sharji Steps Onto the Youth Olympic Stage
detail.excerpt: Backed by two Junior World Cup silver medals in Costa Rica and Bahrain, the young Omani épéeist enters Pool A at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.
detail.article_html:
Inside the Dakar Expo Center in Diamniadio, Senegal, the bouts move fast: five touches or three minutes of active fencing, whichever comes first. When Omani national team fencer Jana bint Mohammed Al Sharji clips into her scoring reel for her Youth Olympic Games debut, she will represent the Sultanate in Pool A of the girls' individual épée competition at Dakar 2026.

For Al Sharji, stepping onto the Olympic piste is the result of months of international competition that have tested her footwork, composure, and timing against older opponents across three continents.

Six Bouts Across Four Continents

Drawn into the seven-fencer first group, Al Sharji faces a diverse opening pool: Ariel Lin of Chinese Taipei, Francesca Aina of Italy, Joana Sabonet of Angola, Senegal's own Ndiaye Mane Mbaye, Olahitan Faridat Fassassi of Benin, and Ghazal Madani of Iran.

In the round-robin pool stage, each fencer meets every opponent in the group in a race to five touches—or a one-minute priority overtime if the score stands level after three minutes. Pool rankings then seed the direct elimination bracket beginning with the Round of 16 on the same day, leading straight through to the semi-finals and medal bouts.

Two World Cup Silvers on the Road to Senegal

Al Sharji arrives in Dakar with strong international momentum. In the weeks leading up to the Games, she captured two silver medals on the Junior World Cup under-17 circuit. Her first podium came on October 22 in San José, Costa Rica, where she strung together three consecutive knockout victories—winning 15–8, 15–13, and 12–6—to reach the final.

Less than two weeks later, on November 5 in Manama, Bahrain, she claimed her second World Cup silver medal after defeating fencers from Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Kyrgyzstan, and Hong Kong, before also advancing to the quarter-finals of the Asian Under-23 Fencing Championship in Bahrain.

National fencing coach Hisham Karshoud, who oversaw Al Sharji's final training camp in Bahrain before departing for Senegal, notes that while several competitors in the Dakar draw are older, Al Sharji's recent international schedule has sharpened both her technical precision and her tactical patience under pressure. Her appearance concludes Oman's campaign at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, which brings together roughly 2,650 young athletes from 204 National Olympic Committees across 153 events.

Sources

  • Oman Daily
detail.instagram_caption:
Omani national fencing team athlete Jana bint Mohammed Al Sharji is set to make her Youth Olympic Games debut in the girls' individual épée competition at Dakar 2026 in Diamniadio, Senegal. Drawn into the seven-athlete Pool A, she will face competitors from Chinese Taipei, Italy, Angola, Senegal, Benin, and Iran for a place in the direct elimination rounds.

Al Sharji arrives in Senegal on the back of two Junior World Cup Under-17 silver medals won in late October and early November. In San José, Costa Rica, she recorded three consecutive knockout victories to reach the final, followed days later by a second World Cup silver in Manama, Bahrain, and a quarter-final finish at the Asian Under-23 Fencing Championship.

Coached by Hisham Karshoud, Al Sharji's appearance marks the culmination of an intensive international preparation calendar and concludes Oman's participation at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games alongside 2,650 athletes from 204 National Olympic Committees.
